description: Two repetitions at each of 1600/1700/1800/1900 offered TPS, ascending then descending order. Five-second offered windows; four validator processes and one client share an 8-logical-CPU macOS AArch64 host. Real signatures, durable group commit (64 requests / 1 ms), 20 ms one-way delay, 5 s deadline, max in-flight 16384, inline verification. No deliberate concurrent builds/tests/profiling during measurements. Short-run queueing investigation, not a sustained capacity guarantee. Throughput includes drain. Client outstanding/cohort analysis reconstructed afterward from outcome traces.

report.measurement_definition: Signed transaction submission before transport enqueue to client receipt and strict Ed25519 verification of effects QC; client generation/signing excluded; network queues, fixed per-direction delay, validator validation/signing and group sync_all before votes included.
report.limits: One host, loopback TCP, fixed one-way delay without packet-loss/bandwidth modelling; one hot collective pool; bounded journal group commit; filesystem/device sync_all guarantees assumed. Finalized latency percentiles are conditional; all-submitted quantiles include right-censored stalls.

client_outstanding.description: Reconstructed from submission plus certificate-verification time; censored stalls would use5sdeadline. This measures client outstanding work across all stages, not a specific validator queue.

bottleneck_interpretation: Validator service wall-time increasingly comprises blocking journal write/sync calls; events per sync decline and mean barrier cost rises at higher offered loads. Operation, Effects and Final requests share one FIFO state worker. Per-queue enqueue/dequeue residence and per-round client processing delays were not instrumented, so exact latency attribution and the causal reason for batch-size/barrier changes remain unproven. Service totals are not a decomposition of client critical-path latency.
